(ou: a segunda metade do caso mais famos: (or: the second half of the most famous case in Russian)
Onde você está agora. Você aprendeu, na: Where you are now. In lesson 27 you learned the genitive singular, the "of" and the negation. You can already say: У меня́ нет кни́ги. (I have no book.) Э́то дом ма́мы. (It is Mum's house.) У меня́ нет вре́мени. (I have no time.) Now the second half. In this lesson you will learn: STEP 1: the genitive plural, how to say "I have no books" (нет книг). STEP 2: numbers, how to say "two books" (две кни́ги) and "five books" (пять книг). STEP 3: the prepositions of the genitive: без, для, до, из, от, у. After this lesson you will have finished the essential grammar of Russian, because you will have seen all 6 cases. I explain that at the end. The genitive plural works like the singular, but with different endings. English plurals just add -s; Russian plural endings depend on the gender and the last letter, and in the genitive plural many feminine and neuter nouns lose their ending completely. Here are the main rules, and I will go through each case with examples.
Masculino em ж, ч, ш, щ: Masculine in ж, ч, ш, щ
O masculino no genitivo plural: The masculine in the genitive plural
O masculino no genitivo plural. Masculin: The masculine in the genitive plural. Hard masculine → -ОВ. Notice: you add -ОВ to the end of the word. It is the most common masculine rule. Watch the irregulars: друг → друзе́й (not "другов"). Брат → бра́тьев (not "братов"). These are exceptions you will learn by heart. Soft masculine (-ь, -й) → -ЕЙ (and -ЕВ after -й). Notice: the -ь or -й disappears and -ЕЙ comes in. Masculine in ж, ч, ш, щ → -ЕЙ. Notice: after ж, ч, ш, щ the ending is -ЕЙ (not -ОВ).
O feminino no genitivo plural: The feminine in the genitive plural
O feminino no genitivo plural. Feminino: The feminine in the genitive plural. Feminine in -а → no ending. Notice: the -а disappears and the word is just the stem, with no ending at all. This is the most frequent feminine plural, but it is not always so simple; see the next topic on the fleeting vowel. Feminine in -я → -Ь. Notice: the -я disappears and -Ь (the soft sign) comes in, or a fleeting vowel appears. Feminine in -ь → -ЕЙ. Notice: the -ь disappears and -ЕЙ comes in. Feminine in -ия → -ИЙ. Notice: the -я disappears and -ИЙ comes in (with two "i"s, one of them the letter й).
O neutro no genitivo plural: The neuter in the genitive plural
O neutro no genitivo plural. Neutro em -: The neuter in the genitive plural. Neuter in -о → no ending. Notice: the -о disappears. Sometimes a fleeting vowel appears (о́кон, пи́сем; see the next topic). Neuter in -е → -ЕЙ. Notice: the -е disappears and -ЕЙ comes in (words in -ие take -ИЙ instead: упражне́ний). Neuter in -мя → -ЁН. Notice: these 10 or so words are neuter and end in -мя. In the genitive plural they become -ЁН (with a stressed ё).
A vogal eufônica: o segredo do plural fe: The fleeting vowel: the secret of the feminine and neuter plural

The fleeting vowel: the secret of the feminine and neuter plural. This is one of the rules that confuse learners most, yet it is predictable once you see the logic. When the stem ends in two consonants, a vowel (о or е) is inserted between them in the genitive plural to make the word easier to say. The logic: Russian dislikes hard consonant clusters at the end of a word, so it adds a vowel. English does the same thing when it says "film" as "fil-um" or "athlete" as "ath-a-lete". Examples with о and with е follow below. A practical rule: before the last consonant, after ж, ч, ш, щ (and after ь or й) you usually get -ЕК (кошек, девочек); after other consonants you usually get -ОК (палок, окон). Careful: there are exceptions. If in doubt, check a dictionary. The most common words you will end up memorising. Examples in sentences:
Os numerais russos se formam somando, da: Russian numerals are built by adding, from the biggest part to the smallest: 21 = двадцать один; 35 = тридцать пять; 148 = сто сорок восемь. From 13 to 19 you add -надцать to the base (тринадцать). The tens from 50 to 80 have a -ь- in the middle: пятьдесят, шестьдесят, семьдесят, восемьдесят. Watch 40 (сорок) and 90 (девяносто), which are special. Hundreds: сто, двести, триста, четыреста, пятьсот, шестьсот, семьсот, восемьсот, девятьсот.
Conte de 10 em 10 até 100 e diga: «двадц: Count by tens up to 100 and say: «двадцать пять, тридцать семь, сорок девять, сто двадцать».

Os irregulares mais comuns do plural. Ex: The most common irregular plurals. Some words have an irregular genitive plural, and you have to memorise the main ones. Notice: some end in -ЬЕВ (братьев, деревьев, перьев, крыльев), others in -ЕЙ (друзей, мужей, детей, людей), and others have no ending (яблок, денег, суток). Keep these, because they come up all the time in daily life. English has irregular plurals too (man/men, child/children, foot/feet), so this is the same kind of memory work.
A grande aplicação: os NÚMEROS. Agora ch: The big application: NUMBERS. Now we reach the most practical part of the genitive plural, and one of the most famous rules in Russian. The number 1 goes with the nominative singular. The numbers 2, 3 and 4 go with the genitive singular. The numbers 5 and up go with the genitive plural. English only has "one book" and "two or more books"; Russian has three groups. Let us see it with the word "book" (кни́га). Notice: the genitive singular is used with 2, 3, 4, and the genitive plural with 5+. Then with "table" (стол) and with "window" (окно́). Notice: the pattern is always the same. 1 → nominative singular. 2-4 → genitive singular. 5+ → genitive plural. The "last number" rule: when the number is compound, the last number decides. That is why Russian is logical: the last number of the sequence decides. Examples in sentences follow. The forms of "1" and "2" for each gender. The number 1 and the number 2: notice that the number 2 has два (masculine/neuter) and две (feminine). That is an important distinction. The numbers 3 and 4 do not change with gender: три, четы́ре.
As preposições do genitivo. Agora, as pr: The prepositions of the genitive. Now the prepositions that take the genitive. These are the most important. I will explain each with examples. БЕЗ: without. Notice: the object after без goes into the genitive. ДЛЯ: for. Notice: the object after для goes into the genitive. ДО: until, before. ИЗ: from (origin). Notice: из shows origin, where something comes out of. Do not confuse it with от, which shows moving away from a person. ОТ: from (moving away). Notice: от is used with people (moving away from them). Из is used with places (origin). У: at, by, at someone's place. Notice: у is already familiar from the "have" sentences (у меня́ есть). Here it means "by" or "at someone's place". О́КОЛО: near. КРО́МЕ: except. ПО́СЛЕ: after.
junto a, em casa de: at, by, at the home of
O substantivo muda conforme o número. De: The noun changes with the number. After 1 (and 21, 31...): nominative singular: один студент, двадцать одна книга. After 2, 3 and 4 (and 22, 23, 24...): genitive singular: два студента, три книги, четыре окна. After 5 to 20 and after 25, 30...: genitive plural: пять студентов, десять книг, двадцать окон. The numerals 1 and 2 have gender: один / одна / одно; два / две (feminine). Age: «год» with 1 (21 год), «года» with 2 to 4 (22 года), «лет» with 5 and up (25 лет); from 11 to 14 it is always «лет».
em português só mudamos para o plural a: English only switches to the plural from 2 on, and only has two forms ("one book", "two books"). Russian has three rules: 1, 2 to 4, and 5 and up.
Diga: «Мне … лет. У меня две сестры и од: Say: «Мне … лет. У меня две сестры и один брат. В книге сто двадцать страниц.»
Quantidade e tabelas de apoio no genitiv: Quantity and support tables for the genitive plural
A grande aplicação: a QUANTIDADE. Certas: The big application: QUANTITY. Certain words of quantity take the genitive. The most important are in the table below. Notice: all of them take the genitive, always. Examples in sentences follow. The rule: мно́го, ма́ло, немно́го, ско́лько, сто́лько and не́сколько always take the genitive. And is it the genitive singular or plural? It depends on the word. Uncountable words (са́хар, вода́, вре́мя) → genitive singular (мно́го са́хара, ма́ло вре́мени). Countable words (кни́га, стол, дом) → genitive plural (мно́го книг, ма́ло столо́в). It is the same split English makes between "much" and "many": if the thing is countable, plural; if uncountable, singular. Erros comuns e frases no genitivo plural: Common mistakes and sentences in the genitive plural
Os erros que o brasileiro VAI cometer no: The mistakes English speakers WILL make with the genitive plural. Mistake 1: using the singular after «нет» when the thing is plural. Wrong: У меня́ нет кни́ги. (singular, but you meant several books) Right: У меня́ нет книг. (plural) You learned the genitive singular in lesson 27 and tend to use it everywhere. But when the thing is plural, the genitive is plural. Mistake 2: adding -ОВ to a feminine in -а (instead of dropping the ending). Wrong: У меня́ нет ма́мов / кни́гов. Right: У меня́ нет мам / книг. Mistake 3: forgetting the -ОВ on a hard masculine. Wrong: У меня́ нет стол. Right: У меня́ нет столо́в. A hard masculine takes -ОВ. Mistake 4: using -ОВ on soft or sibilant stems that need -ЕЙ. Wrong: У меня́ нет учи́телов / врачо́в. Right: У меня́ нет учителе́й / враче́й. Mistake 5: forgetting the fleeting vowel. Wrong: У меня́ нет ко́шк. Right: У меня́ нет ко́шек. The fleeting vowel is obligatory when the stem ends in two consonants. Mistake 6: mixing up the number rules. Wrong: У меня́ пять кни́ги. Right: У меня́ пять книг. 5+ takes the genitive PLURAL, not the singular. It is one of the most confused rules. Mistake 7: forgetting that 2, 3, 4 take the genitive SINGULAR. Wrong: У меня́ две книг. Right: У меня́ две кни́ги. 2, 3, 4 take the genitive SINGULAR, not the plural. It is the opposite of the previous mistake. Mistake 8: forgetting that 1 goes with the nominative. Wrong: У меня́ одна́ кни́ги. Right: У меня́ одна́ кни́га. 1 goes with the nominative singular. It is the only number that does not take the genitive. Mistake 9: using the wrong gender with the number 2. Wrong: два кни́ги. Right: две кни́ги. Два is masculine/neuter. Две is feminine. Кни́га is feminine, so две. Mistake 10: forgetting the genitive after БЕЗ, ДЛЯ, ДО, ИЗ, ОТ, У. Wrong: без са́хар. Right: без са́хара. Wrong: для ма́ма. Right: для ма́мы. All the prepositions of the genitive take the genitive, always. Full sentences with the genitive plural. Here are real sentences.

Fechamento da gramática essencial e quad: Closing the essential grammar and summary of the genitive
A tranquilização final: você terminou a: A final word of reassurance: you have finished the essential grammar. Now a pause. Listen to what I am about to say. You have finished the essential grammar of Russian. You have now seen all 6 cases: STEP 1: Nominative, the case of the subject. STEP 2: Accusative, the case of the action. STEP 3: Prepositional, the case of place. STEP 4: Dative, the case of things that happen to you. STEP 5: Instrumental, the case of the extensions of the body and of "with". STEP 6: Genitive, the case of possession, origin and negation. You already know the alphabet. The gender of nouns. The gender of adjectives. Verbs in the present, past and future. Personal pronouns, possessives and demonstratives. Numbers. The main prepositions. And here is the truth nobody tells you: the hard part of Russian is over. The learner's mistake is to think the advanced stage is the hard one. In Russian the hard part is the basic structure, because it is abstract, full of rules and full of exceptions. You faced that part and you won. What comes next is not harder, it is richer. After the genitive, Russian opens up into vocabulary (thousands of new words), idioms (learning to talk like a Russian), culture (understanding why Russians say what they say) and immersion (reading books, listening to music, watching films, talking with Russians). All of that is much easier than grammar, because it is intuitive, cultural and alive. You already have the structure. Now you build the house. One thing is left: practice. Read, listen, speak, write, every day, even if only for 15 minutes, because structure only consolidates with use. Summary table: the genitive plural.
Os ordinais são adjetivos: concordam com: Ordinals are adjectives: they agree with the noun. Masculine: первый, второй, третий...; feminine: первая, вторая, третья...; neuter: первое, второе, третье.... «Третий» is special (третья, третье, третьи). To give the date, use the ordinal in the NEUTER and the month in the GENITIVE: «первое мая» (1 May, "the first of May"). To say "on" a date, the ordinal also goes into the genitive: «первого мая» (on 1 May). Uses: floor («на третьем этаже»), order («второй урок»).
Today is the first of May.
My birthday is on the tenth of June.
